summary: Christy Doran contrasts the Springboks, who are portrayed as playing for South Africa, with the All Blacks, who are portrayed as playing for themselves and for a departing generation of leaders, ahead of the 2023 Rugby World Cup final. He recalls Rassie Erasmus's 2019 'ego' speech and Jacques Nienaber's selection philosophy. He then covers the All Blacks' motivation after the Ireland series loss, the 'Last Dance' farewells, and Ian Foster's departure after 12 years.
one_line: Ahead of the 2023 World Cup final, the Springboks play for South Africa while the All Blacks play for themselves and their departing leaders.
key_facts: Before the 2019 World Cup final, Rassie Erasmus told the Springboks they had no right to worry about their mistakes, saying 'If you worry about your mistakes today, you've got ego problems.'
The Springboks beat England 32-12 in the 2019 final to claim their third William Webb Ellis Cup.
Jacques Nienaber announced two changes to his starting side, five in total, and went with a forwards-heavy 7-1 bench split.
Nienaber said selection is 'for South Africa', not about person or ego.
The Springboks reached the 2023 final after consecutive one-point victories in the knockout stages.
The All Blacks' social media managers had to delete a thousand comments an hour after the historic home series loss to Ireland, which ended 2-1 in Ireland's favour, with the final loss in Wellington.
In August the All Blacks suffered their biggest defeat to the Boks and lost the inaugural Qatar Cup.
Dalton Papali'i said senior players opened up and showed vulnerability, with some tears, giving others 'an extra two, three per cent'.
The All Blacks' social media described the final team selection as the 'Last Dance'.
Dane Coles will retire, while Brodie Retallick and Sam Whitelock will head overseas; Whitelock is bidding to be the first player to win the Webb Ellis Cup three times.
Aaron Smith and Beauden Barrett will head to Japan after the World Cup.
Coles, 36, missed selection for the final; Ian Foster called telling him the toughest conversation he has had as a coach.
Foster will leave the All Blacks after 12 years, the last four as head coach, and Scott Robertson has been announced as his successor.
A 35-23 win over the Springboks at Ellis Park helped Foster save his career after historic defeats to Argentina and the Ireland series loss.
